# `prefer-loop-else`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: none · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a boolean flag whose only purpose is to remember that a loop broke
before fallback work.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

A loop `else` branch directly expresses work that runs only when iteration
completes without `break`.

## When it fires

The loop body must consist only of a matching `if` that sets the flag and
breaks, followed immediately by an `if (!flag)` fallback. Flags read afterward
are excluded.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn contains(items: []const u32, needle: u32) bool {
    var found = false;
    for (items) |item| {
        if (item == needle) {
            found = true;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (!found) return false;
    return true;
}
```
